source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Resting on fairly weak established clinical rationale for combining these two particular medications together in most clients","B":"Being used mainly in situations where spironolactone alone happens to already be contraindicated for that particular client","C":"Achieve effective diuresis while helping maintain more stable potassium levels, since the two medications have complementary effects on potassium","D":"Causing significant hyperkalemia in most clients who end up receiving this particular combination of medications together"}}
source_row.rationale: Combining furosemide (which can cause potassium loss) with spironolactone (which is potassium-sparing) in a specific ratio helps achieve effective diuresis for ascites while helping maintain more stable potassium levels, leveraging the complementary electrolyte effects of these two medication classes.
source_row.source_name: AASLD — Combination Diuretic Therapy in Ascites
